title: Fin locomotion: Strouhal band and Bainbridge line, whole species held out
converted_by: tracks/suite/make-cases.mjs; numbers are the agent's own, times are file times, see the header of that script

statement.text: A: cruising swimmers have St = f*A/U in [0.2, 0.4], with A the peak-to-peak tail amplitude. B: tail-beat frequency is linear in length-specific speed, f = a + b*(U/L), with the Bainbridge form f = 4/3 + (4/3)*U/L. The checked repo file tracks/research/lean/hv-morph-fin-locomotion__FinLocomotion.lean (PASS in CHECKED.txt) states St = a*k and only bounds St to [0.15, 0.5] from the kinematic windows; it does not state the 0.2-0.4 band or statement B. items.what: The law: the 0.2-0.4 band is not universal. About 1 in 5 adult cruising records fall outside; carangiform swimmers in the development set are inside only 47% of the time; larval zebrafish sit at 0.72-2.5; the one adult zebrafish clip is at 0.71. St also falls with speed (Spearman -0.40 development, -0.33 held-out), so a fixed band ignores a real trend.
